ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AM$ is the bisector of $\angle CAB$, and $CN$ is the bisector of the exterior angle $\angle GCB$. $BE \perp AM$ at point E, and $BD \perp CN$ at point D, with $DE$ connected. If $AB=4$, $BC=5$, and $AC=6$, what is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, \\
extend $BE$ to meet $AC$ at point $F$, and extend $AC$ and $BD$ to meet at point $G$,\\
since $AM$ bisects $\angle CAB$ and $BE\perp AM$,\\
it follows that $\angle CAM=\angle BAM$, $\angle AEF=\angle AEB=90^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle AFE=90^\circ-\angle CAM$, $\angle ABE=90^\circ-\angle BAM$,\\
hence $\angle AFE=\angle ABE$,\\
which implies $AF=AB$,\\
given that $AB=4$, $AC=6$, and $BC=5$,\\
it follows that $FC=AC-AF=AC-AB=6-4=2$,\\
since $CN$ bisects $\angle GCB$ and $BD\perp CN$,\\
it follows that $\angle GCN=\angle BCN$, $\angle CDB=\angle CDG=90^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle CGD=90^\circ-\angle GCN$, $\angle CBD=90^\circ-\angle BCN$,\\
hence $\angle CGD=\angle CBD$,\\
which implies $CG=CB=5$,\\
therefore $FG=FC+CG=2+5=7$,\\
since $AF=AB$ and $BE\perp AM$,\\
it follows that $AE$ is the median to side $BF$, that is, point $E$ is the midpoint of $BF$,\\
since $CG=CB$ and $BD\perp CN$,\\
it follows that $CD$ is the median to side $BG$, that is, point $D$ is the midpoint of $BG$,\\
thus $DE$ is the midsegment of $\triangle BFG$,\\
therefore $DE=\frac{1}{2}FG=\boxed{\frac{7}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached geometry diagram shows triangle ABC with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, and C above. The line AC is extended beyond C to a point labeled G. A ray from A passes through the interior point E and continues to M, representing the angle-bisector line AM. A ray from C passes through D and continues to N, representing the exterior-angle-bisector line CN. The right-angle marks indicate BE is perpendicular to AM at E and BD is perpendicular to CN at D; segment DE is drawn/connected. Reasoning: Extend BE to meet AC at F. Since AM bisects angle CAB, reflecting ray AB across AM gives ray AC. Because BE is perpendicular to AM and passes through B, the intersection F on AC is the reflection of B across AM. Therefore AF = AB = 4, and E is the midpoint of BF. Since AC = 6, FC = AC - AF = 6 - 4 = 2. Next, CN bisects the exterior angle GCB, so reflecting ray CB across CN gives ray CG. Since BD is perpendicular to CN, extending BD to meet the AC extension at G makes G the reflection of B across CN. Hence CG = CB = 5, and D is the midpoint of BG. The points F, C, and G are collinear, with C between F and G, so FG = FC + CG = 2 + 5 = 7. In triangle BFG, E is the midpoint of BF and D is the midpoint of BG, so DE is a midsegment. Therefore DE = FG/2 = 7/2.
